description:
An open letter to the American people from Iran's Revolutionary Guards (IRGC) claims the US public don't know what is happening in Iran and asks them to pressure the Trump administration to end the war.
 
Meanwhile President Donald Trump has said he believes taking action against Tehran will be seen as one of the most important things in the history of the United States.
 
Iran threatens to attack infrastructure across the Middle East, if the country's security cannot be guaranteed.
 
And there's a warning from the head of the International Energy Agency that Europe faces a difficult winter for energy supplies.

description:
Andy Burnham delivers first his speech to the Labour Party conference as Prime Minister. During an emotional address, the prime minister outlined plans for a ‘National Care Service’ which would be free at point of use, funded in part by proposed changes to the triple lock" from 2030.

He also talked about reforms to the electoral system and housing, and the water system.

The Prime Minister received a long standing ovation when he teared up speaking about his late father, who died just a few weeks ago.

Christa Pike was 20 when she became the youngest woman on death row in the US. 

Now, 30 years later she’s facing her execution date this week. She would be the first woman put to death in Tennessee in nearly 200 years. 
 
Pike was one of two people convicted of brutally beating, torturing and murdering Colleen Slemmer, a 19-year-old woman she met at a training programme for troubled teens.

author: BBC News
description:
The Premier League has confirmed that Manchester City have been found guilty of all charges related to breaches of Premier League financial rules between 2009-10 and 2017-18.
 
An independent Commission found that during that time period, the club arranged "sham contracts" with a number of its commercial partners, as well as "relying on sham agreements to artificially inflate the club's revenues and reduce its costs".
 
The statement also said that City were guilty of the majority of charges in relation to its failure to co-operate.
 
Meanwhile, a City statement said the club was "both disappointed and surprised by the opinion of the Premier League Commission".
 
"The Club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case," the statement said.
 
The statement added that Manchester City FC will now pursue the appeal avenues open to it.

Subscribe to our channel here
title: Manchester City guilty of all charges related to financial rules, Premier League confirms | BBC News

author: BBC News
description:
Lives "will be lost" unless the UK does more to prepare for wildfires, experts warn, after a record-breaking summer saw 1,350 wildfires in England and Wales alone.
 
"Tinderbox" conditions created by a long, hot, dry summer brought the worst wildfire season on record in 2026.
 
Dozens of homes were destroyed or damaged, huge areas of land burned, and one man died. 
 
The UK government banned disposable barbecues, sent a wildfire alert to people's mobile phones and made £97m available, and a wildfire summit is planned - but are we still behind the curve?
 
In this episode of Behind the Investigation, Melanie Stewart-Smith speaks to Adrian Goldberg from File on 4 Investigates about what he found on the ground.

1:34 Stourbridge: A couple lose their home
3:45 The man who died fighting a Cotswolds fire

author: BBC News
description:
Spain's coalition government has approved new housing measures following protests over the country's housing crisis, sparked by the eviction of an 87-year-old woman from her home in Madrid last week.

Ministers met on Tuesday to discuss the proposals, which include a potential ban on evictions until 2030, Health Minister Mónica García said.

She said the measures would bring relief to more than five million people - but opposition politician Míriam Nogueras said the agreement left "small landlords out in the cold”.

The new housing measures need to be approved in parliament, where the leftist coalition government lacks a majority.

description:
Ukraine's National Academy of Sciences was hit by a Russian drone strike, killing one person and leaving three injured, according to city's mayor Vitaliy Klitschko.
 
Footage showed people leaning out of windows as they evacuated the burning building.
 
Firefighters helped people evacuate through the windows as a plume a black smoke billowed out of the building.
 
The BBC's diplomatic correspondent Paul Adams was at the scene as emergency services attempted to stop the raging fire.
 
Russia has been carrying out sustained attacks on Ukraine, with explosions reported in the capital Kyiv in the early hours of Tuesday morning, with several buildings damaged.

OpenAI has announced it will not release its latest AI model due to safety concerns.
 
Its GPT-6.1 Astra system, which performs tasks like browsing the web and using apps by itself, "didn't quite meet the bar" of the company's standards, according to Saachi Jain, head of safety systems at OpenAI.
 
It comes as breaches by major AI firms' models intensify the debate about risks posed by the tech - with Anthropic underlining its concerns AI might threaten humanity as it prepares to go public.

description:
Brits seeking mental health support are travelling overseas for psychedelic therapy.
 
The treatments involve substances such as psilocybin and ayahuasca, both of which are illegal under UK law.
 
At the same time, researchers are conducting clinical trials to investigate whether something similar could have a place here. 
 
While campaigners argue the treatments could transform care, further evidence is needed and significant regulatory hurdles remain.

author: BBC News
description:
New York state prosecutors say they will reopen a criminal inquiry into the alleged rape of a woman at Cornell University in 2024.
 
The woman filed a civil lawsuit on 16 September alleging she was drugged and raped by multiple people at a fraternity house at the university.
 
"Once we determine the appropriate charges, the case will be prosecuted in the most objective and impartial means possible" through a grand jury, Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten said Monday.
 
Cornell University said that while it supported the case being brought before a grand jury, "any suggestion that the university did not impose consequential punishments for those involved is false".
